Structure: Entity: LLC or benefit corp owned by... the entity itself (nonprofit shell?) or founding board that has zero profit rights (profits legally must flow to workers). Member relationship: Not "owners" - more like "active participants with voting rights" Deposit ($200) = launch capital, returned as meal credits or refunded if you quit No equity, no ownership stake, no capital account Profit distribution (monthly vote): Each month, surplus gets voted on: Option A: Distribute to that month's workers (proportional to hours worked) Option B: Save for specific goal (voted at yearly meeting) Option C: Hybrid split Example month: $40K surplus Option A: $40K ÷ 1,500 hrs = $26.67/hr bonus (on top of $20 base wage embedded in meal value) Option B: All $40K → expansion fund Option C: $20K distributed ($13.33/hr bonus), $20K saved Yearly meeting: Vote on: Savings goals for next year (2nd location? heated delivery system? pay down debt faster?) Platform cooperative (collective ownership, no individual equity) Members collectively own LLC No individual equity shares Profits flow to collective, distributed by vote Can be nonprofit or for-profit Cleanest fit for what you're describing I'd go with #3: Platform cooperative model How it works: Founding: 200 members × $200 deposit = $40K + $60K loan = $100K equipment LLC formed, owned collectively by "active member class" No individual shares, no equity accounts Governance: Active member = worked 8+ hrs in last 60 days, gets 1 vote Inactive member = worked <8 hrs in last 60 days, loses vote but can reactivate Decisions: Monthly (profit distribution), Yearly (big stuff), Emergency (safety/legal) Profit distribution: Default: 50% distribute to month's workers, 50% save Can be changed by monthly vote (requires 50%+1) Distribution formula: (Your hours that month ÷ Total hours that month) × Distribution pool Expansion funded by surplus: Want 2nd location?
